import pandas as pd, statsmodels.formula.api as smf
df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
print(df.describe().T[['count','mean','std']])
print(df.corr(numeric_only=True)['remote_share'])
base="patents_per_100_eng_2023 ~ remote_share"
pre=" + log_engineers_2020 + firm_age_2020 + patents_per_100_eng_2020"
pre2=pre+" + vc_backed + founder_ceo + cloud_spend_2020 + hq_in_hub_city + share_phd_2020 + gross_margin_2020 + C(region)+listed+C(segment)"
for name,f in [("raw",base),("pre",base+pre),("pre+collab",base+pre+"+collab_index_2023"),("pre2",base+pre2),("pre2+collab",base+pre2+"+collab_index_2023")]:
    r=smf.ols(f,df).fit(cov_type="HC1")
    print(name,r.params['remote_share'],r.bse['remote_share'],r.pvalues['remote_share'],int(r.nobs))
r=smf.ols("collab_index_2023 ~ remote_share"+pre2,df).fit(cov_type="HC1")
print("collab on remote",r.params['remote_share'],r.pvalues['remote_share'])

{"decision":"reject","reason":"The reported -2.73 effect comes from controlling for collab_index_2023, a 2023 post-treatment variable (remote_share raises it, coefficient 0.60), which induces collider/mediator bias. Without it, the estimate is about -0.28 (p=0.24, not significant), with or without the full set of pre-period covariates, so the 'negative effect' conclusion is not robust. The analyst also ran only one specification."}

content.text:
I rejected the report's conclusion. I wrote the decision to `verdict.json`.

The analyst's "negative effect" of -2.73 depends on one control, `collab_index_2023`. That index is measured in 2023, after the remote-work period. Remote share raises it (coefficient 0.60 when I regressed the index on remote share), so it sits downstream of the treatment. Controlling for it biases the estimate. The analyst's justification, that it "captures an important determinant of the outcome", doesn't fix this.

I did not re-run the analyst's `analysis.py` itself. I re-estimated the models with my own script, `rep.py`, and my version with the collaboration control gave -2.91 (SE 0.23) on all 2,000 firms. The analyst trimmed the top and bottom 1% of the outcome (N = 1,960), so the -2.73 and -2.91 aren't directly comparable. The same robust standard errors (HC1) were used throughout.

| Specification | remote_share coefficient | p-value |
|---|---|---|
| No controls | 1.60 | about 0 |
| Pre-2020 controls (size, age, prior patents) | -0.28 | 0.24 |
| All pre-2020 covariates, plus region, listed and segment | -0.28 | 0.25 |
| Pre-2020 controls plus `collab_index_2023` | -2.91 | about 0 |
| All pre-2020 covariates plus `collab_index_2023` | -2.89 | about 0 |

Without the collaboration index, the effect is small and not statistically distinguishable from zero. The analyst also estimated only one specification and did not check how sensitive the result was to this choice.
